Title: Documented end-user setup-to-first-slideshow path (no Rust)
Requirement: The system shall enable an end user to produce a first playable MP4 by following the documented end-user path only: run the setup script (SR-024) once, edit one TOML config, run one `build` command — with no Rust/compiler toolchain, no source checkout, and no source-code edits required of the end user.
Rationale: Removes the setup friction UN-001 says causes abandonment before first output; enforces the UN-021 audience split so a non-programmer is never routed into installing Rust.
AcceptanceCriteria: On a clean Windows host with NO Rust toolchain installed: following only the documented end-user quick-start — (1) run the setup script which installs/locates FFmpeg and places the prebuilt binary (SR-023/SR-024), (2) edit a single TOML file, (3) run one `build` — yields ≥1 MP4 that plays; no documented end-user step installs Rust/a compiler, requires a source checkout, or instructs editing `.rs` source. Building from source is a separate Developer path (SR-025), never part of these end-user steps.

Title: Pre-run validate gates build on runtime prerequisites only
Requirement: The system shall provide a `validate` command that checks each essential RUNTIME prerequisite (FFmpeg present on PATH, config parses, media_root readable, output base_dir writable) and reports each as a plain-language pass/fail, and `build` shall refuse to start when any essential prerequisite fails; `validate` shall NOT check for or require a Rust/build toolchain, FFmpeg being the sole external runtime dependency.
Rationale: Implements UN-002 so a missing/typo'd runtime prerequisite is caught before a long run rather than after; FFmpeg is the only runtime dependency (the binary is already in hand per UN-019), so a Rust/build toolchain is never treated as a prerequisite.
AcceptanceCriteria: `validate` emits one labeled pass/fail line per checked runtime prerequisite in plain language; when any essential check fails, `validate` and `build` both exit non-zero without producing output; when all pass, `validate` exits zero; no checked prerequisite is a Rust/compiler/build-toolchain check, and `validate` succeeds on a clean machine that has FFmpeg + valid config + readable/writable paths but no Rust installed.

Title: Single documented config file with defaults and units
Requirement: The system shall be configured by one TOML file in which every user-facing field has a documented default and stated unit, and the documented defaults shall require no understanding of codec/CRF/Ken Burns internals to produce frame-friendly output.
Rationale: Implements UN-003 so a non-programmer can configure a run by editing plain settings only.
AcceptanceCriteria: For each field in `[[outputs]]`/`[input]`/`[output]`/`[processing]` the docs state a default and unit; loading a config that omits all optional fields succeeds using those defaults; the default-produced output satisfies SR-005.

Title: Build progress and completion summary
Requirement: The system shall report ongoing progress during `build` (items processed of total per stage) and, on completion, emit a summary listing each output file written with its path, or a clear failure message when no valid output was produced.
Rationale: Implements UN-004 so long unattended runs are visibly alive and the user knows the result and where outputs landed.
AcceptanceCriteria: During `build`, progress updates showing processed/total are emitted as work proceeds; on success the final summary lists every written output path; on failure a plain-language message is emitted and exit code is non-zero.

Title: Frame-compatible default encode profile
Requirement: The system shall, with default settings, produce H.264 video in an MP4 container with pixel format yuv420p, `+faststart`, even width and height, and frame rate within 24-30 fps inclusive.
Rationale: Implements UN-005: pins the broadly compatible profile so default output plays on budget frames, not just the PC.
AcceptanceCriteria: ffprobe of a default-config output reports codec=h264, container=mp4, pix_fmt=yuv420p; the moov atom precedes mdat (faststart); width%2==0 and height%2==0; 24<=fps<=30.
Permutations: codec=h264; container=mp4; pix_fmt=yuv420p; faststart=on; fps={24,25,30}; dims=even

Title: Even-dimension enforcement for any configured resolution
Requirement: The system shall encode each output at its configured resolution and shall ensure the encoded width and height are both even for every supported panel resolution.
Rationale: Decomposes the even-dimension requirement of UN-005 across the multiple panel resolutions UN-007 allows, since yuv420p H.264 rejects odd dimensions.
AcceptanceCriteria: For each resolution in Permutations, the encoded stream's width and height are even and match (or are the even-adjusted form of) the configured values; encoding never aborts due to odd dimensions.

Title: Frame-rate bounds
Requirement: The system shall accept a configurable output frame rate and the documented default shall fall within 24-30 fps inclusive.
Rationale: Implements the fps portion of UN-005 so default output stays within the range budget panels support.
AcceptanceCriteria: Default-config output has 24<=fps<=30; a configured fps within the supported set is honored in the encoded stream as reported by ffprobe.

Title: Quality/bitrate via CRF default
Requirement: The system shall control output quality via an H.264 CRF parameter whose documented default lies in the 26-30 range recommended for smooth playback on budget frames.
Rationale: Implements the bitrate/smoothness guidance of UN-005 so default output neither stutters on weak decoders nor bloats file size.
AcceptanceCriteria: The default `quality_crf` is within 26-30 inclusive; the configured CRF is passed unchanged to the H.264 encoder; lowering CRF measurably increases output file size on identical input.

Title: Pre-run oversize (FAT32 4GB) size estimate and warning
Requirement: The system shall estimate each output's duration and file size before/while building and shall emit a warning naming the affected output when its estimated size exceeds ~3.5 GB, and shall surface any output whose final size exceeds that threshold (path + size) in the completion summary.
Rationale: Implements UN-006 (pre-run guard) and the UN-018 edge case so the user is warned about the 4 GB FAT32 wall before and after, not when the frame rejects the card.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given a config/media whose estimated output exceeds 3.5 GB, `build` emits a warning naming the output and pointing to documented mitigations; any final output file > 3.5 GB is listed with its path and size in the summary; estimate uses the documented duration formula (sum of clip durations minus transitions x fade_time_secs).

Title: Source media never modified
Requirement: The system shall open all input media read-only and shall never create, modify, move, or delete any file under the configured media_root.
Rationale: Implements the UN-013 guarantee that a crash/power loss can never corrupt source media.
AcceptanceCriteria: After any `build`, `validate`, `stats`, or `bench` run (including a run interrupted mid-execution), every file under media_root is byte-for-byte unchanged (verified by pre/post hash) and no files are added or removed there.

Title: Crash-safe output (no complete-looking partial)
Requirement: The system shall write each output via a temporary/in-progress file that is atomically promoted to its final `<name>.mp4` name only after a successful encode, so that a run killed mid-write leaves no partial file bearing the final output name.
Rationale: Implements UN-013 and UN-016: a partial output must be distinguishable from a finished MP4 so the user is never misled by a truncated file.
AcceptanceCriteria: If `build` is killed before an output completes, no file with the final `<name>.mp4` name exists for that output (only a distinguishable temp/in-progress artifact, if any); re-running after a kill completes normally without double-producing or silently skipping outputs.

Title: FFmpeg-missing detection
Requirement: The system shall detect when FFmpeg is not available on PATH and shall fail with a plain-language message naming FFmpeg as the cause and a non-zero exit status, without attempting a build.
Rationale: Implements UN-014 for the FFmpeg-missing case so the failure is loud, named, and actionable.
AcceptanceCriteria: With FFmpeg absent from PATH, `validate` and `build` print a message identifying FFmpeg-not-found and a fix hint, produce no output file, and exit non-zero.

Title: FFmpeg-error handling with no false success
Requirement: The system shall surface a non-zero FFmpeg exit or encode failure as a plain-language error naming the affected file/output and shall itself exit non-zero, never reporting success when no valid output was produced, and shall abort a stalled FFmpeg process after a configurable inactivity timeout (default 120 s with no encoder progress/output) rather than waiting indefinitely.
Rationale: Implements UN-014 for the FFmpeg-error case so the user is never told a failed run succeeded, and bounds a wedged FFmpeg so an unattended run cannot block forever.
AcceptanceCriteria: When FFmpeg exits non-zero during an output, the tool reports the failing output/file and the error, exits non-zero, and lists no successfully-written file for that output. If FFmpeg produces no progress/output for longer than the inactivity timeout (default 120 s, configurable), the tool aborts the FFmpeg process, reports the timeout naming the affected output, and exits non-zero — i.e. the run always terminates within (work time + one timeout interval), never hanging indefinitely.

Title: Corrupt/unsupported input skip-and-continue
Requirement: The system shall, by default, skip an input file it cannot read/decode, log the skipped file path and the reason, continue processing remaining files, report the total skipped count in the completion summary, and define exit status by whether any valid output was produced: exit zero when ≥1 valid output is written, exit non-zero with a plain "no outputs produced" message when every input was skipped (zero valid outputs).
Rationale: Implements UN-015 so one bad file never aborts a long run and the user can decide whether to re-source skipped items; the all-skipped case must fail loudly so an empty run is never mistaken for success.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given a media set containing ≥1 unreadable/unsupported file alongside valid files, `build` completes, produces output from the valid files, logs each skipped file with a reason, and the summary states the skipped count; the run exits zero when at least one valid output was produced. When EVERY input is skipped (zero valid outputs), `build` exits non-zero and emits a plain-language "no outputs produced" message rather than exiting zero.

Title: Storage-full detection without complete-looking output
Requirement: The system shall detect a write failure caused by insufficient disk space for output or temporary data, stop with a plain-language out-of-disk-space message naming the path, fail the run with a non-zero exit, and not leave a finalized output file that appears complete.
Rationale: Implements UN-016 so a full disk fails loudly instead of silently producing an unusable truncated file.
AcceptanceCriteria: When the output/temp volume cannot accommodate the write, the tool emits an out-of-space message naming the path, exits non-zero, and no file with the final output name is left for the affected output.

Title: Output/input path missing or unwritable handling
Requirement: The system shall detect when the configured output base_dir (or input media_root) is missing or unwritable before/at write time, report the specific path and the problem in plain language, and stop cleanly with a non-zero exit rather than crashing cryptically or writing nowhere.
Rationale: Implements UN-017 so removed/unwritable SD/USB/NAS paths produce a clear, path-named failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: With output base_dir removed or read-only (or media_root missing), the tool names the exact path and the problem, exits non-zero, and produces no silently-discarded output; the failure is a plain message, not an unhandled panic/stack trace.

Title: Multiple output definitions per run
Requirement: The system shall accept multiple `[[outputs]]` definitions in one config and produce one MP4 per definition in a single `build`, each honoring its own resolution, fps, and quality.
Rationale: Implements UN-007 so a user with several frames produces all targets in one run instead of re-running per frame.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given N output definitions, one `build` writes N distinct MP4s (one per definition); ffprobe confirms each output's resolution/fps match its definition.

Title: Case-insensitive ignore list
Requirement: The system shall exclude files and folders whose path matches any configured ignore pattern, matching case-insensitively.
Rationale: Implements UN-008 so private albums are kept off the frame regardless of letter case.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given ignore_patterns and a media set, no file whose path contains a pattern (matched case-insensitively) appears in the scanned media or any output; non-matching files are still included.

Title: Honest capability/gap reporting
Requirement: The system's documentation shall mark not-yet-implemented Rust-engine features (audio, `bulk_video_time_min` part-splitting) as unimplemented and direct the user to the PowerShell pipeline or a workaround where the Rust engine falls short.
Rationale: Implements UN-009 so the user is not surprised mid-project by a missing feature.
AcceptanceCriteria: The README/quick-reference explicitly label audio and `bulk_video_time_min` splitting as not implemented in the Rust engine and name the PowerShell path/workaround; no doc claims these Rust features work today.

Title: Single discoverable quick-reference
Requirement: The system documentation shall provide one canonical quick-reference (the core commands and the recommended frame settings) that is discoverable from the README, with all other docs linking to it rather than restating its values.
Rationale: Implements UN-010 (fast re-entry) and UN-011 (single source) so the few key facts exist in exactly one place.
AcceptanceCriteria: A quick-reference containing the commands and recommended starting settings exists and is linked from the README; the recommended-settings values appear in exactly one location and other mentions link to it.

Title: No conflicting restated constraints across docs
Requirement: The system documentation shall state each output constraint/setting value once and reference it elsewhere, with no constraint restated with a conflicting value across docs.
Rationale: Implements UN-011 so the user never sees the same setting explained with different values.
AcceptanceCriteria: An inspection of README/roadmap/spec/quick-reference finds no constraint or setting (resolution set, fps range, CRF default, 3.5 GB threshold) given conflicting values; shared facts are stated once and linked.

Title: Deterministic reproducible output
Requirement: The system shall produce equivalent output when re-run on unchanged media with an unchanged config, using deterministic per-file Ken Burns parameters seeded from the file path.
Rationale: Implements UN-012 so the user can compare results across config tweaks without chasing random pan/zoom changes.
AcceptanceCriteria: Two `build` runs over identical media and identical config produce per-clip Ken Burns motion that is identical (same path-seeded pan/zoom/rotation parameters); differences attributable only to non-deterministic encoder timing, not to motion.

Title: Self-contained prebuilt binary distribution
Requirement: The system shall be distributed as a self-contained prebuilt Windows binary (`slideshow.exe`) published via GitHub Releases, whose only external runtime dependency is FFmpeg, and which requires no Rust toolchain, build tools, or source checkout to run.
Rationale: Implements UN-019 so a non-programmer can download-and-run; the engineering realization of the end-user run path in SR-001.
AcceptanceCriteria: A prebuilt `slideshow.exe` asset is published on a GitHub Releases page; on a clean Windows machine with FFmpeg present but NO Rust toolchain or build tools installed, the downloaded binary runs `validate` and `build` to completion (producing a playable MP4) using only the binary + FFmpeg; the binary requires no .NET/Rust runtime install beyond FFmpeg.

Title: Setup script installs/locates deps and self-elevates
Requirement: The system shall provide a single setup script that installs or locates FFmpeg, fetches and places the prebuilt binary (SR-023), self-elevates to administrator when an action requires it, verifies FFmpeg is present afterward, and reports success or a plain-language failure naming what to fix — requiring no Rust toolchain.
Rationale: Implements UN-020 so the manual download/copy/PATH friction UN-001 warns about is replaced by an installer that "just works" (precedent: InstallDependencies.ps1/.bat).
AcceptanceCriteria: On a clean Windows host: running the documented setup script ends with FFmpeg locatable and the `slideshow` binary placed/locatable, then prints a clear success message; the script requests elevation itself when an action needs admin (no manual "Run as administrator" guesswork); it is idempotent (a second run on an already-set-up host succeeds without error or duplicate install); on failure it exits non-zero with a plain-language message naming what to fix; it never requires or installs Rust. Re-running verifies FFmpeg present afterward in both elevation states.

Title: End User vs Developer documentation audience split
Requirement: The system documentation shall present two clearly separated paths: an End User (run) path — setup script + FFmpeg + prebuilt binary, with no Rust — and a Developer (build-from-source) path requiring the Rust toolchain + FFmpeg, with the end-user quick-start containing no Rust/compiler step.
Rationale: Implements UN-021 so the audience split is explicit and a non-programmer is never accidentally routed into installing Rust; coordinated with the UX docs (SR-019/SR-020/SR-021).
AcceptanceCriteria: Inspection of README/quick-reference shows the End User (run) path and the Developer (build-from-source) path as distinct, labeled sections; the End User quick-start steps reference only the setup script (SR-024), FFmpeg, and the prebuilt binary (SR-023) and contain no Rust/`cargo`/compiler step; any Rust/`cargo` build instructions appear only under the Developer section.
